previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, a transplanted pancreas and kidney, mechanical mitral valve, and peripheral vascular disease was admitted for revascularization of a non-healing left lower extremity ulcer. She had previously developed pneumonia during a prior admission, delaying the procedure. This time, her pulmonary status had improved, and a chest X-ray showed resolution of the prior infiltrate. She underwent successful left popliteal artery stenting with restoration of blood flow. The procedure was uncomplicated, and her left foot remained warm with dopplerable pulses. Anticoagulation was managed with IV heparin and bridging to coumadin, with fresh frozen plasma given preoperatively due to elevated INR. She remained afebrile, with stable vital signs and no signs of infection. She was discharged to extended care on IV heparin, aspirin, and coumadin, with plans for vascular surgery follow-up in four weeks.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with INR 10.1, now with vomiting and severe
headache // Please assess for acute intracranial processes, ie bleed

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial MDCT images were obtained through the brain
without the administration of IV contrast. Reformatted coronal, sagittal and
thin section bone algorithm-reconstructed images were then generated.

DOSE:  CTDIvol: 54.81 mGy

DLP: 891.93 mGy-cm

COMPARISON:  Comparison is made to CT head dated ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is no evidence of acute intracranial hemorrhage, edema, mass effect, or
large territorial infarction. The ventricles and sulci are normal in size and
configuration. The basal cisterns appear patent and there is preservation of
gray-white matter differentiation.

The visualized bony structures are grossly unremarkable. A large, left
maxillary mucous retention cyst is noted. The remainder of the paranasal
sinuses, mastoid air cells, and middle ear cavities are otherwise clear. Dense
atherosclerotic mural calcification of the bilateral vertebral and internal
carotid arteries is noted. A left globe prosthesis is noted. The right globe
is unremarkable.

IMPRESSION: 

No evidence of acute intracranial process.

INDICATION:  Pain with history of chronic osteomyelitis.

COMPARISON:  ___ CT abdomen/pelvis.

ONE VIEW PELVIS AND SEVEN VIEWS OF THE LEFT LOWER EXTREMITY INCLUDING THE
FEMUR AND TIBIA/FIBULA:

There are mild degenerative changes of both femoroacetabular joints.  No acute
fracture is appreciated.  Bones are demineralized.  There are heavy vascular
calcifications.  A stent is noted within the popliteal region.  No osseous
destruction or aggressive-appearing periosteal reaction.  

IMPRESSION:  No radiographic evidence of osteomyelitis or acute fracture.  If
there is continued clinical concern for osteomyelitis or fracture, consider
MR.

EXAMINATION:  Lower extremity arterial study with rest

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with significant PVD and chronic osteomyelitis
with L foot ulcer/cellulitis // Please assess arterial flow in legs given plan
to amputate L toe

TECHNIQUE:  Doppler waveforms, segmental blood pressure measurements and pulse
volume recordings in the lower extremities.

COMPARISON:  None

FINDINGS: 

Right leg:

Triphasic waveform in the common femoral, superficial femoral, and popliteal
arteries. There is transition to a monophasic waveform below the knee, in the
posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis arteries. Monophasic flow was also was
detected in the right digit. Diminished pulse volume recordings below the
knee. The ankle-brachial index at rest is 0.72.

Left leg:

Monophasic waveform in the common femoral, superficial femoral artery,
popliteal and dorsalis pedis artery. No flow detected in the posterior tibial
artery. Diminished pulse volume recordings below the knee. The ankle-brachial
index is inaccurate due to non compressible vessels around the ankle. Using
the toe / digital pressure, the ABI would be estimated at 0.48. There is
minimal flow in the left when compared to the right.

IMPRESSION: 

1. Severe aortoiliac and tibial disease on the left. The posterior tibial
artery is occluded. There is some dampened flow in the dorsalis pedis artery
and minimal flow in the left toe when compared to the right.

2. The findings on the right suggest a patent femoral - posterior tibial
bypass graft with moderate disease of the native vessels below the knee.
